title: Inheritance: reuse, `super` and the limits of a hierarchy

videos.script: A library lends books and DVDs. Both have a title, a year and a loan period, and only the book has an author. {{extends}} This lesson writes the shared part once, in a class called Item, and lets Book and Dvd extend it. A book gets describe for free. A DVD replaces one method and keeps the rest. {{super}} Then the two uses of super. One calls the parent's constructor, and it has to come first. The other calls the parent's version of a method you are replacing. {{object}} Then the class at the top of every hierarchy, Object, and the three methods everything inherits from it. Two of them give a surprising answer for two identical books. {{limits}} Last, where inheritance stops paying. One parent only. The is-a test. And a set that counts six additions for three ISBNs, because of code in a class it did not write. By the end you can extend a class, and you know when to hold a field instead.
